module_title: Isotopes, Isobars, and their Modern Applications
introduction: In nature, not all atoms of the same element are identical. They can have different masses. This level covers isotopes, isobars, and their critical applications in modern medicine, energy, and archaeology.

core_concepts.title: Isotopes
core_concepts.description:
Atoms of the SAME element having the 'Same Atomic Number (Z)' but a 'Different Mass Number (A)'. 
Reason: They have the same number of protons but a 'different number of neutrons'. 
Example: Carbon isotopes (C-12, C-13, C-14).

core_concepts.title: Isotopes of Hydrogen
core_concepts.description:
Hydrogen has 3 famous isotopes (highly tested in exams): 
1. Protium ($^1H_1$): 1 Proton, 0 Neutrons (Normal water). 
2. Deuterium ($^2H_1$): 1 Proton, 1 Neutron (Used to make 'Heavy Water' - $D_2O$). 
3. Tritium ($^3H_1$): 1 Proton, 2 Neutrons (It is 'Radioactive').

core_concepts.title: Isobars
core_concepts.description:
Atoms of DIFFERENT elements having the 'Same Mass Number (A)' but a 'Different Atomic Number (Z)'. 
Example: Argon ($^{40}_{18}Ar$) and Calcium ($^{40}_{20}Ca$). Both have a mass of 40 but are different elements.

core_concepts.title: Isotones
core_concepts.description:
Atoms of different elements containing the 'Same number of Neutrons'. 
Example: Carbon-14 ($^{14}_6C$) and Oxygen-16 ($^{16}_8O$). Both have exactly 8 neutrons ($14-6=8$ and $16-8=8$).

important_entities.name: Properties of Isotopes
important_entities.significance: Because chemical properties depend purely on electrons (Atomic Number), isotopes have 'identical chemical properties'. However, because their masses differ, their physical properties (like density and boiling point) are slightly different.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
These 4 applications appear in almost every exam. Memorize them: 
1. Uranium-235 ($U-235$): Used as fuel in nuclear reactors. 
2. Cobalt-60 ($Co-60$): Used in radiotherapy for Cancer treatment. 
3. Iodine-131 ($I-131$): Used to treat Goiter (Thyroid disorders). 
4. Carbon-14 ($C-14$): Used for Carbon Dating to find the age of fossils.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: IsoTOPE = Top number is different. IsoBAR = Bar (weight/mass) is same.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Isotopes have different top numbers (Mass). Isobars have the same mass.

exam_strategy_tips: NDA/PCS Question: 'Which isotope of hydrogen is radioactive?' Answer: Tritium.
